notes:
Lead profile: Benchcast Support (benchcast.ai) — mid-stage SMB building an AI-native helpdesk layer on top of Zendesk/Front. Inbound came from blog + quickstart, self-serve signup. Primary contact: Maya Lin, VP Product (calls). AE: Daniel Park; SE: Anika Rao.

Use-case summary:
- Core ask: automated ticket summarization + triage. Want one-call workflow that extracts: issue_type, urgency, impacted_product, recommended_assignee, short_summary (1-2 lines), and structured metadata for downstream automation.
- Also exploring tool-calling to trigger internal automations (create/update ticket, add label, escalate). Need function/tool calling examples (they called this out explicitly).
- Want structured output (JSON schema) to plug into existing workflows. Lots of emphasis on deterministic keys and stable schema.

Performance & cost constraints:
- Latency expectation: 150-500ms per token for 95p on short summaries (they measure from ingest to response). Will accept slightly higher p99 for batch rerank jobs.
- Throughput: peak ~120 reqs/min during high volume windows, average 10-20 reqs/min. Cost-sensitive: want to keep monthly spend under $5k initially.
- Model preference: open to Redwood-curated open models; will evaluate both smaller/quantized variants for cost and occasional higher-quality model for edge cases.

Security & compliance:
- Public cloud OK for now. Need SSO (SAML) for admin access and audit logging for ticket transformations. No strict residency requirement currently.

What we demo'd / POC plan:
- Ran a quick PoC on hosted API using Zendesk export sample. Built a mapping to their ticket schema and produced structured outputs that matched their internal fields.
- Next POC: 1) demonstrate tool-calling flow (create-ticket + add-priority), 2) show structured-output stability across noisy ticket text, 3) cost/runbook for batching & caching.

Quotes / call snippets:
- "We need the output to be predictable — our automation will fail if keys shift." — Maya Lin
- "We signed up because quickstart was simple. If the hosted API gives predictable latency and schema, we can roll into prod in 8-10 weeks." — Engineering lead (Jordan)
